note: All cases target the disposable PM-Sandbox project (Nexusdev, id 70844de4-391c-4002-ac3c-6f1e21e4ecd3) so runs never touch the real backlog. Fixtures: NEX-129 daemon loop (unready), NEX-130 assembly (ready), NEX-131 CI PATH fix (ready, small, time-sensitive), NEX-132 dep-ordering (unready), NEX-133 rename cutover (partial), NEX-134 gh-304 (ready; dedup target).

evals.prompt: Prioritize the backlog in the PM-Sandbox project (Nexusdev team) in Linear and set the issue priorities.
evals.expected_output: A stack rank with a visible ICE score (Impact, Confidence, Ease and the product) per issue, each mapped to a Linear priority bucket, followed by proposed priority writes that wait for confirmation before touching Linear.
expectations: Shows a per-issue ICE breakdown with Impact, Confidence, and Ease values AND the multiplied score, not just a bare ordering
Maps each issue to a Linear priority level (Urgent/High/Medium/Low or 1-4)
Proposes the priority writes and explicitly waits for user confirmation instead of calling save_issue immediately
Reads the live PM-Sandbox issues before proposing, rather than assuming
Does NOT compute RICE or WSJF for these individual issues (uses ICE as the default single-scorer framework)

evals.prompt: A new bug is proposed for the PM-Sandbox project (Nexusdev): 'github client throws on a 304 from gh api instead of treating it as unchanged'. Triage it.
evals.expected_output: A triage decision that separates severity from priority, searches existing PM-Sandbox issues for a duplicate (finds NEX-134) before creating anything, and gives an accept/defer/delete call with a reason — all proposed before any Linear write.
expectations: Distinguishes severity from priority explicitly rather than conflating them into one number
Searches existing issues for a possible duplicate before proposing to create anything, and surfaces the near-duplicate (NEX-134)
Gives an explicit accept / defer / delete decision with a stated reason
Proposes any label/priority/relation writes and waits for confirmation before executing

evals.prompt: Write a Linear story in the PM-Sandbox project for adding automatic retry-with-backoff to the github read client.
evals.expected_output: A story that is a vertical slice with a user/operator-facing outcome, has 3+ testable Given/When/Then acceptance criteria, is scoped to a single AI build session, and is proposed as a Linear issue before being created.
expectations: Frames the story as a vertical slice with a user- or operator-facing outcome, not a component/task like 'add a retry function'
Includes at least 3 testable acceptance criteria in Given/When/Then form
Explicitly checks or states that the story is sized to complete in one AI build session (splits or flags it if not)
Proposes the issue for confirmation before calling save_issue

evals.prompt: The PM-Sandbox project has a pile of backlog issues but no roadmap. Plan one in Linear.
evals.expected_output: A Now/Next/Later roadmap organized by decreasing certainty, mapped onto Linear initiatives/projects, that flags the PM-Sandbox project is not linked to an initiative, and proposes the structure before writing it.
expectations: Organizes the roadmap into Now / Next / Later horizons of decreasing certainty rather than fixed dates
Maps horizons onto Linear initiatives and/or projects (not just an inline text list)
Flags that the PM-Sandbox project is not linked to an initiative (disconnected roadmap gap)
Proposes the initiative/project changes and waits for confirmation before writing

evals.prompt: Nexusdev now runs 2-week cycles. Plan the current cycle for the PM-Sandbox backlog.
evals.expected_output: A cycle plan that fills the cycle with the top-ICE ready stories up to a rough capacity budget, treats the cycle as a cadence bucket (flow continues; not a frozen scope), pulls only ready stories (NEX-130/131/134, not the unready NEX-129/132), and proposes the cycle assignments before writing.
expectations: Selects stories for the cycle by ICE rank up to a rough throughput/capacity budget, rather than dumping the whole backlog in
Treats the cycle as a cadence bucket, not a frozen commitment (states that flow continues / overflow can be pulled early, does not freeze scope)
Only pulls ready stories into the cycle and excludes the unready ones (NEX-129 daemon loop, NEX-132 dep-ordering have no acceptance criteria)
Proposes the cycle assignments and waits for confirmation before calling save_issue with the cycle param
